definition: A large, publicly available repository of web-crawled data, widely used as a raw data source for pretraining large language models.
details: Common Crawl provides petabytes of web page data collected over many years, and is typically filtered, deduplicated, and cleaned extensively before being used in LLM pretraining pipelines.

explainer.lead: Common Crawl is a huge public collection of web pages gathered over many years. It gives AI teams a vast starting pool of text, but turning that raw material into useful language-model training data takes extensive cleaning.

tiers.eli5: Imagine a giant library filled with copies of pages from across the web, built up over many years. Before using those pages to teach a language model, people remove repeats and unwanted material, much like sorting and cleaning a messy box of papers.
tiers.practitioner: Teams use Common Crawl as raw input to LLM pretraining pipelines rather than as a ready-made training corpus. At petabyte scale, filtering, deduplication, and cleaning are central pipeline stages; skipping or weakening them leaves more duplicate and unwanted web material in the training data.
tiers.paperLevel: Let C denote Common Crawl's repository of web pages collected across many crawls. A pretraining corpus can be represented as D = Clean(Deduplicate(Filter(C))), with substantial processing required before D is suitable for LLM pretraining.

explainer.example: A team building a language model selects Common Crawl pages, removes duplicate documents, filters and cleans the remaining text, and uses the resulting corpus for pretraining rather than training directly on the raw crawl.

usedIn.name: Large language model pretraining
usedIn.detail: A widely used source of raw web text for building pretraining corpora.

usedIn.name: Web-data processing pipelines
usedIn.detail: Crawl data is filtered, deduplicated, and cleaned before training use.

explainer.intuition: Common Crawl is like a vast raw supply of web pages: plentiful and publicly accessible, but not automatically clean or training-ready.
howItWorks: Collect web pages across many crawls over many years.
Store the resulting petabyte-scale data in a public repository.
Filter the raw data to select material for training.
Deduplicate and clean the selected pages extensively.
Feed the processed text into an LLM pretraining pipeline.
explainer.whyItMatters: It makes an enormous amount of web data publicly available, providing raw material for language-model development at a scale that would otherwise require collecting and storing web pages independently.
misconceptions: It is not a clean, ready-to-use LLM training set.
It is a data repository, not a language model.
Using it does not remove the need for filtering, deduplication, and cleaning.
